title: Custom Slack App vs Buying Another Tool: When to Build vs Buy
description: A framework for deciding when to build a custom Slack app instead of buying another SaaS tool. Learn when custom Slack apps, workflows, and automation make sense for fintech and ecommerce teams.
excerpt: Every founder hits this fork eventually: a process breaks down, and the instinct is to shop for a SaaS tool to fix it. Sometimes that's right. But we've watched startups stack 15+ tools that don't talk to each other — while the team still lives in Slack all day anyway.
keywords: custom software vs off the shelf

sections.heading: Buy a Tool When
sections.content: Buy when the workflow is standard (payroll, basic CRM, invoicing), you need it live this week not next month, and the process isn't part of your actual differentiation.

sections.heading: Build When: Your workflow IS the differentiator
sections.content: A fintech client had a fraud-review process that didn't map onto any off-the-shelf platform. We built a Slack app with approve/deny buttons and a full audit trail inside Slack — no context-switching, no second login.

sections.heading: Build When: Paying full price for a fraction of the product
sections.content: If your team touches 20% of the features on a $40K/year platform, a scoped custom Slack app is usually cheaper to build AND maintain than the license, onboarding, and admin overhead combined.

sections.heading: Build When: Decisions need to happen where data already lives
sections.content: For an ecommerce brand, order exceptions buried in a dashboard nobody opened. We moved that logic into Slack: alerts fire where ops already works, with one-click actions to resolve on the spot.

sections.heading: Build When: Scaling a manual process that breaks with headcount
sections.content: If someone on your team is the integration layer between two disconnected tools — copy-pasting, cross-checking — that's a build signal, not a hiring signal. A custom Slack app eliminates the bottleneck entirely.

sections.heading: The real question isn't build vs. buy
sections.content: It's: does this workflow touch how you make money or serve customers in a way that's genuinely specific to you? If yes, a generic tool will always be a compromise. If no, buy it and move on.

faq.question: When should I buy a SaaS tool instead of building a custom Slack app?
faq.answer: Buy when the workflow is standard (payroll, basic CRM, invoicing), you need it live this week, and the process isn't part of your actual differentiation. If a generic tool covers the use case without painful workarounds, buying is cheaper and faster.

faq.question: When does building a custom Slack app make more sense?
faq.answer: Build when your workflow is your differentiator, you're paying full price for a fraction of a tool's features, decisions need to happen where data already lives (Slack), or you're scaling a manual process that breaks with headcount.

faq.question: Is a custom Slack app cheaper than buying a SaaS tool?
faq.answer: For teams using only 20% of features on a $40K/year platform, a scoped custom Slack app is usually cheaper to build AND maintain than the license, onboarding, and admin overhead combined.

faq.question: How long does it take to build a custom Slack app?
faq.answer: Simple Slack apps with a single workflow typically take 1 to 2 weeks. More complex apps with multiple integrations or AI agents can take 4 to 8 weeks.
